namelist_definition.entry: Default: .true. If .true., eatm will run
Default: ' ' Full pathname of eatm domain file

Which emulator's channel layout to use. Selects the input/output channel table in eatm_channels_mod.F90; it must match the checkpoint that eatm_model_file was traced from (compare against the *_metadata.yaml the tracing script writes next to the .pt file). Default: ACE2-EAMv3
Full pathname of the traced TorchScript emulator (.pt) that FTorch loads. Produced by the ACE tracing script with --add-normalization --add-corrector (and --device cuda for a GPU run). Default: ' '

Full pathname of the emulator initial-condition file, read on a startup run. Must contain one 2D (lat, lon) field per emulator input channel, named exactly as the channel is named in the checkpoint. Ignored on a continue/branch run, where the state comes from the eatm restart file. Default: ' '
Device FTorch loads the traced model onto. Must match the device the model was traced for. Default: gpu

If .true., append the checkpoint's "next step forcing" channels to the input tensor after the state block. Only needed when the traced graph actually consumes them (i.e. when it was traced with --add-ocean); the correctors do not. The traced graph slices the state block off the front either way, so .false. is safe for a model traced without --add-ocean. Default: .false.

If .true., reproduce the pre-review surface diagnostics: Sa_z from a standard atmosphere pressure altitude above sea level, Sa_shum set to the saturation specific humidity at the lowest layer, precipitation phase split on a 273.15 K lowest-layer temperature threshold, and Faxa_swnet reported as the downwelling surface shortwave. Provided only so earlier runs can be reproduced. Default: .false.

Height at which the atmospheric state handed to the coupler is valid.
near_surface: use the emulator's predicted near-surface diagnostics (Tat2m, Qat2m, Uat10m, Vat10m) at a 10 m reference height, with Sa_pbot = Sa_pslv. This is the convention datm uses to force the same ocean and sea ice from JRA (the IAF_JRA_1p5 datamode), so an EATM run and a GMPAS-JRA1p5-2023 baseline present the surface-flux scheme with states at the same height. Silently falls back to lowest_level for an emulator with no near-surface channels, such as ACE2-EAMv3.
lowest_level: use the lowest model layer's mean state at the layer midpoint. For an 8-level ACE grid that midpoint is ~450 m up, which is far above the constant-flux layer that shr_flux_atmOcn's similarity theory assumes.
Default: near_surface

If .true., the specific humidity handed to the coupler is capped at its saturation value for the exported temperature and pressure.
shr_flux_atmOcn treats Sa_shum as the vapour mixing ratio and drives the latent flux with (q_sat(SST) - Sa_shum), so a supersaturated value suppresses or reverses evaporation.
This matters most in the lowest_level configuration, where the exported field is the emulator's specific *total* water and includes condensate: 19.3% of ocean cells arrive supersaturated, with relative humidities up to 2.82. No emulator channel separates vapour from condensate, so capping at saturation is the closest estimate of the vapour part the model's own output supports. In the near_surface configuration Qat2m is a true vapour humidity and the cap acts only as a guard.
Ignored when eatm_legacy_surface is .true., which sets the humidity to saturation by construction. Default: .true.

Seed for libtorch's random number generators, applied once at initialization.
The SamudrACE-E3SMv3 atmosphere is a NoiseConditionedSFNO and draws random noise on every forward pass, so without a seed two runs of identical code diverge. That spread was measured at order 5 W/m2 in the ocean's net surface heat flux over 20 days -- larger than most changes worth testing -- which made the emulator effectively impossible to A/B.
The seed actually applied is eatm_rng_seed + the coupler step number at initialization. Seeding with the same value in every segment of a resubmitted run would replay one noise realization per segment; with 1-year segments that is a spurious annual periodicity. Adding the step number keeps a run reproducible -- it is fixed by the seed and the start date -- while letting the sequence continue rather than repeat.
A negative value leaves the generators unseeded, which reproduces the behaviour before this option existed.
Note this makes a cold start reproducible; it does not make a restart bit-reproducible against a continuous run, because the generator state itself is not carried in the restart file.
Has no effect on ACE2-EAMv3, which is deterministic. Default: 0

Height in metres reported as Sa_z for the exported atmospheric state, used only when eatm_surface_layer = 'near_surface'.
10 m matches what datm hands this ocean and sea ice under JRA forcing, so an EATM run and a GMPAS-JRA1p5-2023 baseline present shr_flux_atmOcn with states at the same height.
Exposed because the near_surface export is not internally consistent: Tat2m and Qat2m are 2 m values and Uat10m/Vat10m are 10 m values, and all four are declared at this single height. The height at which the emulator's own learned turbulent flux is valid is not known -- its LHFLX/SHFLX channels are the coupler's fluxes evaluated on EAMv3's lowest model level, around 60 m. Scanning this bounds how much of the emulator/coupler turbulent mismatch the reference height can explain. See REVIEW.md #58 and #59.
Default: 10.0

If .true., the downwelling shortwave handed to the coupler is scaled by the instantaneous insolation over its 6 h window mean, restoring a diurnal cycle the emulator's interval-mean output does not carry.
This is not cosmetic. The emulator's FSDS is a mean over its whole step, and the surface models' albedo is instantaneous and equal to 1 where the sun is down, so a flat 6-hourly shortwave delivers a large share of the ocean's sunlight onto cells the coupler considers night, where it is multiplied by (1 - albedo) = 0 and discarded. Measured on a 10-day ACE2 run: 13.2% of the ocean's shortwave, against 0.3% with the pre-window-mean SOLIN.
The scaling preserves the window mean exactly, since the mean of the instantaneous insolation over the window is that window mean by construction. It is what datm does with an interval-mean shortwave (tintalgo = 'coszen').
Default: .true.

Units of the emulator's frozen_precipitation_rate output channel, used to convert it to the kg/m2/s the coupler expects. Ignored by emulators that do not predict a frozen precipitation rate.
Note that SamudrACE-E3SMv3's variable_metadata declares 'm/s' for both the total and frozen precipitation rates, inherited from EAM's PRECT/PRECS, but the data are in kg/m2/s: the published initial condition has a global mean surface_precipitation_rate of 3.3e-5 (3 mm/day in kg/m2/s; it would be 3.3e-8 in m/s) and a frozen rate of 2.2e-6, i.e. 7% of total precipitation by mass. The traced model's moisture-budget corrector also compares the precipitation channel directly against LHFLX/L_v, which is kg/m2/s. Default: kg/m2/s

Radiation interval in coupler steps, used to tell the coupler which calendar day the surface models should compute albedos for. A negative value is interpreted as an interval in hours. EATM has no separate radiation timestep, so 1 (every coupler step) is the only value that has been exercised. Default: 1

If .true., the land fraction handed to the emulator is the part of the cell no surface model covers (1 - ocnfrac - icefrac - lndfrac, added to lndfrac), and the coupler's merged surface temperature is completed with the emulator's own TS over that same fraction.
This matters because in GMPAS-EATM the land model is a stub, and the driver ships `Sf_lfrac` from `lfrin` rather than `lfrac` whenever the atmosphere and land grids differ (prep_atm_mod.F90:588-594), so the coupler's land fraction is identically zero. The emulator was therefore told the planet had no land and that the surface was at 0 K over 26% of its area.
Setting .false. restores that, and is a diagnostic only. See REVIEW.md #15b and #25. Default: .true.

If .true., SOLIN is the mean top-of-atmosphere insolation over the emulator step about to be taken, evaluated by the midpoint rule on 48 sub-intervals. That is what `cell_methods = "time: mean"` in the E3SMv3 training stream means. If .false., SOLIN is the instantaneous value at the target time, which has the same global mean and an area-weighted RMS difference of 330 W/m2 against a field whose own global mean is 342. Diagnostic only. See REVIEW.md #35. Default: .true.

If .true., the emulator advances at most once per model time (the MCT driver calls atm_init_mct twice without advancing the clock, which used to step the emulator an extra time at startup and leave it permanently 6 h ahead of the coupler), and the lower interpolation bracket at startup is seeded from the initial condition rather than from the first prediction. Diagnostic only. See REVIEW.md #36. Default: .true.

If .true., output channels whose training data carry `cell_methods = "time: mean"` -- every radiative and turbulent flux, the stresses and precipitation -- are held at the upper bracket across the whole emulator interval, because that value already is the mean over it. If .false. they are linearly interpolated from the previous interval's mean, which applies a half-step (3 h) lag to all of them. Diagnostic only. See REVIEW.md #37. Default: .true.

If .true., the emulator is fed its own prediction for the current time (the upper bracket). If .false. it is fed the field last handed to the coupler, which is a partial interpolation between brackets and is not a state any emulator was trained to consume. Diagnostic only. See REVIEW.md #8. Default: .true.
